counterfactual_missing_items: No obvious deposits of IgG, IgA, and C3 to either the epithelial cell surface or the basement membrane zone
Indirect IF using normal human skin and 1-molar sodium chloride–split normal human skin: No IgG and IgA antibodies
Chest, abdomen, and pelvic computed tomography showed no abnormalities
decisive_items: Immunoblotting of normal human epidermal extract: Positive for IgG autoantibodies to envoplakin (210 kDa) and periplakin (190 kDa)
Skin biopsy revealed spongiosis and numerous neutrophils with nuclear dust in the epidermis and superficial perivascular dermatitis with predominant infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis
Flaccid discrete and coalesced bullae, crusts, and erosions over erythematous and cicatricial lesions were present on the face, trunk, and extremities
response.rationale: R4 directly names paraneoplastic pemphigus and is supported by the highly specific positive immunoblotting for envoplakin/periplakin, classic clinical bullous lesions, and characteristic histopathology. R3 is only a broad autoimmune bullous disease umbrella without the specific serologic marker. C1 is a redundant append-only child of R4 that merely restates the same immunoblotting finding; it adds no raw evidence beyond what R4 already covers, and its label is only a modifier of R4. Therefore R4 is the strongest, with a high margin over the vague R3 and no meaningful runner-up among the supplied candidates.

rejected.why: Overbroad category lacking the confirming envoplakin/periplakin autoantibody evidence; it explains the bullous phenotype but not the definitive serologic signature.
Append-only completion that duplicates the key immunoblotting span already cited by R4; it neither adds new raw support nor contests R4.
